title: Magnetic-Field-Calibration-Free Determination of the Hyperfine Constant $A$ in Ultracold Fermi gases of $^{40}$K
authors: Yajing Yang, Biao Shan, Yuhang Zhao, Jiahui Shen, Zhuxiong Ye, Liangchao Chen, Zengming Meng, Pengjun Wang, Wei Han, Jing Zhang, Lianghui Huang
abstract: Hyperfine constant $A$ is a key parameter of the hyperfine structure and underpins precision spectroscopy and metrology. In this Letter, we develop a magnetic-field-calibration-free method for determining the ground-state hyperfine constant $A$ in an ultracold $^{40}$K Fermi gas by utilizing a pair of magnetically insensitive ("clock") transitions. This overcomes the stringent magnetic-field calibration requirements of conventional methods. We measure the transition frequency between these two magnetically insensitive transitions with Hz-level resolution over a range of magnetic fields, and obtain the ground-state hyperfine constant $A = -h\times 285.730536(2)\,\mathrm{MHz}$, corresponding to an absolute uncertainty of about $2\,\mathrm{Hz}$. Our value reduces the uncertainty by nearly three orders of magnitude compared with previous determinations, providing a substantially improved reference for high-precision spectroscopy and metrology with $^{40}$K.
summary: This paper reports a highly precise, magnetic-field-calibration-free determination of the hyperfine constant A for $^{40}	ext{K}$ using ultracold Fermi gases. By measuring the difference between two magnetically insensitive microwave transitions via Ramsey interferometry, the authors significantly reduce the uncertainty in this fundamental constant. This improved reference value is crucial for advancing high-precision spectroscopy and metrology using alkali atoms.
main_problem: The primary goal is to determine the ground-state hyperfine constant A for $^{40}	ext{K}$ with extremely high precision, overcoming the limitations imposed by magnetic field calibration in conventional methods.
main_result: The authors determined the hyperfine constant A = -h x 285.730536(2) MHz, achieving an absolute uncertainty of only about 2 Hz, which represents an improvement of nearly three orders of magnitude over previous measurements.
method: They developed a magnetic-field-calibration-free method by measuring the frequency difference between two magnetically insensitive ('clock') transitions using Ramsey interferometry on an ultracold Fermi gas.
model_or_system: The experiment uses an ultracold Fermi gas of $^{40}	ext{K}$ trapped in an Optical Dipole Trap (ODT). Measurements involve microwave spectroscopy between Zeeman sublevels within the ground-state hyperfine manifold.
key_observables: Transition frequencies ($\omega_\alpha, \omega_ eta$), Ramsey oscillation visibility, and the hyperfine constant A.
important_parameters: The measurement is performed over a range of bias magnetic fields (B) and is designed to be insensitive to magnetic field calibration and atomic density variations.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the AC Stark shift can be accurately removed by extrapolating measurements to zero optical intensity, and the uncertainty budget is calculated by combining contributions from magnetic field fluctuations and AC Stark shifts.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate energy level diagrams, Ramsey oscillation decay curves, and plots showing the measured hyperfine constant A versus magnetic field and ODT intensity, used for systematic correction.
paper_structure: The paper details the use of Ramsey spectroscopy on two insensitive transitions to derive a field-independent expression for A. It then rigorously calculates the total uncertainty budget by propagating errors from magnetic field noise and AC Stark shifts, culminating in the final highly precise value for A.
why_interesting: This work provides a benchmark measurement for fundamental atomic constants in a highly controlled, quantum gas environment. The technique itself—achieving field independence—is a significant methodological advance for precision measurements in AMO physics.
